key_insight: Generation quality depends less on overall sparsity and more on how well the sparse attention mask aligns with the tile-wise geometry of full attention; learning/distilling tile selection preserves quality at high sparsity.
problem_solved: Reduces the quadratic memory/compute bottleneck of self-attention in diffusion transformers for high‑resolution, long video generation, while avoiding quality degradation seen in existing high‑sparsity sparsification methods.
method: Empirical finding: measure and show that tile-wise geometric alignment between sparse masks and full attention determines generation quality.
Distilled sparse attention: formulate explicit tile selection and distill knowledge from dense attention into compact sparse masks so the model learns where to attend.
Integrate the distilled sparse attention into a diffusion transformer backbone to enable scalable high‑resolution, long video generation with much lower compute/memory.
impact: Enables practical scaling of video diffusion models — producing longer, higher‑resolution videos with substantially reduced resource use while maintaining quality. Beneficial for researchers and engineers building efficient generative video systems.
